attribution_limitations: The reference ranges printed in the text (TSH 0.350–4.940 µIU/mL, free T4 0.70–1.48 ng/dL) differ from those in the Table 1 column headers (TSH 0.3–5.0 µIU/mL, fT4 0.7–1.8 ng/dL); the TSH difference is rounding-level and the fT4 upper limit 1.8 versus 1.48 looks like a one-character print artefact.

The text reports one pre-pretreatment TSH (<0.003 µIU/mL) and free T4 (>5 ng/dL), recorded as one item with the Table 1 w/o pretreatment row. The text also says thyroid function tests were repeated at the 4-week visit and presented in Table 1, but does not say which row is that repeat.

Table 1 marks psychotic symptoms with + and − and prints no legend; + is recorded as present and − as absent. The 1-month row is supported by the text that the psychiatric manifestations resolved completely; the 3-month row rests on the table sign alone.

The antithyroid drug withdrawn before RAI and the antipsychotics later discontinued are not named in those sentences; the patient had taken propylthiouracil and was pretreated with methimazole, and the source does not say whether propylthiouracil was replaced.

The time of the 3-month hypothyroidism and levothyroxine start is given as 3 months in the abstract and the 3-month follow-up in the text, without an explicit anchor; Table 1 labels the 3-month row under After RAI.

claims.text: A 30-year-old man with Graves' disease, treated with propylthiouracil and propranolol for about a year, was referred to nuclear medicine in February 2024 after developing acute psychotic symptoms over the preceding month. He was moderately cachectic with an enlarged neck, bilateral exophthalmos, sweating, fine tremors and a heart rate of 125 beats per minute, and had paranoid ideation, hallucinations and disorganized behavior. He reported smoking 12 to 14 cigarettes per day and denied other major illnesses or a family history of hyperthyroidism or psychiatric disorders.
